**Visual Analysis of Test Image:**
- Affected part: corn stalks (multiple stalks shown horizontally)
- Extensive brown/dark necrosis of the outer stalk sheath tissue
- Leaf sheaths are dried, collapsed, and dark brown
- Some small dark spots/lesions visible on the stalk surface
- Some areas show nearly black discoloration
- Overall: stalk rot with external browning and tissue collapse

**Comparison with Anthracnose_stalk_rot reference:**
- The reference shows very similar external browning of the outer stalk tissue (bottom-left panel)
- Internal tissue shows fibrous disintegration with dark lesions (top-right panel)
- The dark spotting and shiny black lesions are characteristic of Anthracnose stalk rot (*Colletotrichum graminicola*)
- The test image matches this pattern — extensive dark brown necrosis of the stalk sheath with black lesion development

The browning pattern, dark discoloration, and tissue collapse on these horizontally-laid stalks is consistent with Anthracnose stalk rot.
